description: Data for deals.html. Every entry must be taken from the retailer's own official page and carry a checked date. status 'link-only' shows a link with no figures. Refreshed by scripts/update_deals.py (see its docstring). Entries may carry an 'expires' date; the page build hides expired entries and expired points/offers.

groups.title: Supermarkets
groups.intro: Loyalty prices, member offers and price-match schemes, as the supermarkets describe them. Most need you to scan a card or app each time you shop.

entries.name: Tesco Clubcard Prices
entries.summary: Tesco says its “Your Clubcard Prices” are personalised offers for eligible customers, based on what they have bought before.
points: New offers arrive in the Tesco app every Wednesday and last for 7 days, to 11:59pm on the following Tuesday.
You have to unlock them in the app or online each week, then scan your Clubcard at the till or link it to your online account.
Tesco's own page says Clubcard Prices may not show in your online basket, but you still pay the Clubcard Price and see it on your receipt.
links: Tesco – expiry dates of Your Clubcard Prices
Tesco – Clubcard Prices not showing in my basket at checkout

entries.name: Sainsbury's Nectar Prices
entries.summary: Nectar Prices are lower prices on a selected range of products at Sainsbury's, in store (not Sainsbury's Local) and online, for Nectar members.
points: In store, scan or swipe your Nectar card or app at the checkout. Online, add your Nectar card to your Sainsbury's account first.
“Your Nectar Prices” are up to 10 personalised offers a week. New ones land each Friday and you have to unlock them before you shop.
Sainsbury's terms say Nectar Prices cannot be applied after the event: if you don't scan or unlock first, you don't get the discount.

expect: scan or swipe your Nectar card or app in-store

entries.name: Asda Rewards
entries.summary: Asda Rewards is an app. Asda says you earn “Cashpot” money by completing missions, such as shopping in certain categories or hitting spending targets.
points: You can convert your Cashpot balance into vouchers to spend in Asda stores and on Asda.com. The money must be spent at Asda and excludes George.com.
Asda's app listing says you have 6 months from the month you earned it to convert your savings before they expire.
Asda's app listing also says you build your Cashpot through missions, not on every item you buy.
links: Asda Rewards on the App Store (Asda's own listing)

entries.name: Morrisons More
entries.summary: Morrisons says More Card members get personalised offers and More Card Prices on selected products when they scan the card in store or online.
points: Morrisons says you earn 5 More Points on every product when you scan your card (the page marks this with an asterisk, so read its terms for exclusions).
When your balance reaches 5,000 points, Morrisons says it gives you a “Fiver” to spend with them.

entries.name: Lidl Plus
entries.summary: Lidl says the Lidl Plus app gives you weekly exclusive offers and personalised coupons, and you collect points when you scan the app as you shop.
points: Points can be spent on rewards in Lidl's Rewards Marketplace.
Lidl says to check the Coupons section of the app for tailor-made coupons and to check the app each week for exclusive offers.

entries.name: Co-op membership
entries.summary: Co-op says members get lower prices on everyday essentials and personalised offers every week, which you choose and then redeem by scanning your membership card online or in store.
points: Co-op says it costs £1 to join, and you get that £1 back on your first shop in store when you select your personalised offer.
Members also choose a local cause to support, and Co-op says the cause gets a share of its profits.

entries.name: Aldi: Price Check and price guarantees
entries.summary: Aldi says it compares its prices with competitors' equivalent products every week. Its Price Check page lists dated “Weekly Price Check” comparisons; when we checked on 26 October 2026, the latest one listed was dated 24 August 2026.
points: Aldi says it regularly monitors competitor prices across the market. Its “Save” page lists Price Drops, Super 6 and Specialbuy Steals.

points.t: Time-limited guarantee (Aldi's own terms): it says it will match the lowest UK supermarket price on pumpkins and squash (excluding multi-buys and promotional prices) between 10 September and 1 November 2026, if you can show proof of a lower price for an equivalent size on the date you buy.

entries.name: “Aldi Price Match” at Tesco and Sainsbury's
entries.summary: “Aldi Price Match” is run by Tesco and by Sainsbury's, not by Aldi. Each matches the price of selected products against comparable Aldi products.
points: Tesco says it matches selected Tesco products against comparable Aldi products, checks Aldi prices in GB stores and/or online twice a week, and doesn't match Aldi promotional prices. The products vary by week, and it isn't in Northern Ireland stores. Tesco now says a selected range of everyday products is price matched in Tesco Express too, not the full range.
Sainsbury's says it covers selected products only, not in Northern Ireland, with prices checked twice weekly. Its terms link to a table of the matched products, which it says is updated regularly.

entries.name: Too Good To Go
entries.summary: Too Good To Go says its app shows which cafes, restaurants, bakeries and stores near you have good food left over, to buy at half the price or less.
points: You reserve and pay in the app, then collect in the pick-up window shown, swiping the app in front of the staff.
Its terms say you can cancel in the app any time before pick-up ends. A reservation isn't a purchase until you collect.
links: Too Good To Go – how the app works
Too Good To Go – how to collect
Too Good To Go – terms and conditions (UK)

expect: half of the price or less

entries.name: My Waitrose
entries.summary: Waitrose says all My Waitrose members can enjoy special savings on a variety of products, online and in store, by using their My Waitrose card.
points: Personalised offers are tailored to each member, so the number and type of offers can vary and there may be times when none are available. You select them in the My Waitrose hub online or in the app, and they apply when you scan your card at checkout.
Waitrose also mentions a free hot drink offer and member-only competitions for members.
“Little Treats”: Waitrose says that each month you spend £50, £100 and £250 earns a Little Treat voucher, up to three a month. You must scan your card in the qualifying shop, and terms apply.
links: Waitrose – My Waitrose benefits and offers

groups.title: Cinema
groups.intro: Memberships, free schemes and 2-for-1 offers, taken from the cinemas' own pages. Ticket prices vary by cinema, film and time, so check your local cinema's page.

entries.name: Cineworld Unlimited
entries.summary: Cineworld says its Unlimited monthly membership lets you see unlimited films, and that the cost depends on your local cinema and which membership group it is in. Check your cinema on its page for the price.
points: You can pre-book up to 5 films at a time, and Unlimited screenings don't count towards that limit.
Members get 10% off in-cinema snacks and drinks, rising to 25% after 3 months, or from sign-up if you pay 12 months upfront (Cineworld says this is the premium Unlimited membership).
All members get 10% off in-cinema Starbucks. Terms apply.

entries.name: ODEON Limitless
entries.summary: ODEON explains how its Limitless membership works in its help centre, and links to the Limitless terms from there. We couldn't read prices from an official ODEON page, so no prices are shown here: please check ODEON's own site.
links: ODEON help centre – Where can I read the Limitless small print?

entries.name: Picturehouse membership
entries.summary: Prices published by Picturehouse for its memberships (all include complimentary cinema tickets, according to its page):
points: Weekday Saver Light: from £6.99 a month or £69.90 a year. Monday to Thursday, all cinemas except Picturehouse Central.
Classic: from £9.99 a month or £99.90 a year. Every day, all cinemas except Picturehouse Central.
Premium West End: from £15.99 a month or £159.90 a year. Any day, includes Picturehouse Central and its Members' Bar.
Picturehouse says members get 10% off food and drink. Its page says the plan you choose is a fixed 12-month membership: read the terms on renewal before you join.

entries.name: Everyman membership
entries.summary: Prices in Everyman's membership terms (all are 12-month terms):
points: Everyman: £95 a year, with 6 membership tickets a year. No monthly plan.
Everyicon: £350 a year, or £31 a month for 12 months, with 24 membership tickets a year.
Everywhere: £680 a year, or £59 a month, with unlimited membership tickets.

entries.name: Vue: Club Vue (free)
entries.summary: Vue says its free Club Vue app gives you a digital stamp with each booking. Once you have 10 stamps you get a free film ticket.
points: Vue says members can self-refund tickets bought online or in the app, up to two hours before the session starts.
Vue also says members unlock free tickets, snacks and drinks as rewards once earned.

entries.name: Meerkat Movies (2 for 1 on Tuesdays or Wednesdays)
entries.summary: Vue and Showcase each publish this scheme on their own sites. It comes from Compare the Market: you claim a voucher code through Compare the Market, then use it at the cinema.
points: Vue says: 2 standard tickets, cheapest free, on Tuesdays or Wednesdays at participating cinemas, with the app-only membership ending on 19 July 2027. Extra charges apply for 3D films and premium seating or auditoriums.

Showcase says: one code per year for Tuesdays or Wednesdays on full-price tickets. It can't be used for Gallery seating or Event Cinema, extra fees apply for 3D, XPlus and XLR seating even on the free ticket, and codes can't currently be redeemed in the Showcase app.

entries.name: Showcase offers
entries.summary: Showcase publishes its current offers on one page.

points.t: Showcase says that until Friday 30 October 2026 you can buy 5 tickets for £25 to use at any Showcase cinema, for any film showing until that date. Terms and exclusions apply, and voucher codes aren't valid for Event Cinema titles.

groups.title: Subscriptions
groups.intro: Prices shown on each service's own UK page. Where a service shows an advert-supported tier, annual plan or student plan, it is listed.

entries.name: Netflix
entries.note: Netflix says plans are billed monthly and it doesn't offer annual, multi-month or lifetime plans. Extra members cost extra.

entries.name: Spotify Premium
entries.note: Spotify says the Student plan switches to Individual (£12.99 a month) when you stop being eligible.

offers.t: Spotify's page says new Premium users get 2 months for £0 on Individual, then £12.99 a month. The offer ends 30 October 2026.

entries.name: Amazon Prime
entries.note: Amazon's page shows a 30-day free trial, after which the subscription continues until cancelled. Prime Video is shown with limited adverts.

entries.name: Disney+
entries.note: Disney+ describes the lower price as based on a 6-month minimum term. Check the page for the terms that apply when you join.

entries.name: Apple Music
entries.note: Apple says there is a free first month for new subscribers, and that the Student plan comes with Apple TV at no extra cost.

entries.name: Apple TV

expect: £9.99 per month after a free 7-day trial

entries.note: Apple says Apple TV is free for three months if you buy a new Apple device and redeem the offer within 90 days.

entries.name: NOW (Sky)
plans: Entertainment Membership after the minimum term
entries.note: NOW says the Entertainment Membership auto-renews at £7.99 a month after the minimum term unless you cancel, and that standard memberships include adverts.

entries.name: YouTube Premium
entries.summary: YouTube shows its plans and prices on its own page. We couldn't read the prices from an official page automatically, so none are shown here.

groups.title: High street
groups.intro: Loyalty schemes and member offers from high-street chains, as they describe them.

entries.name: M&S Sparks
entries.summary: M&S says Sparks gives you offers: you activate an offer, shop, and earn a reward once you reach the spend target.
points: You activate an offer by selecting “Activate offer”. M&S says the page then shows whether the target has to be met in one transaction or across several.
M&S says rewards for fashion, home and beauty purchases show as pending for 14 days to allow for returns.

entries.name: B&Q Club
entries.summary: B&Q says that when you scan your B&Q Club card every time you shop, it emails you money-off coupons for future shops.
points: B&Q says that if you register to receive offers by email, it sends your first coupon: £5 off when you spend £30 or more.

expect: £5 off when you spend £30 or more

entries.name: Club Pret
entries.summary: Pret says Club Pret gives you 50% off up to five hot or iced barista-made drinks a day, for £5 a month. The page marks “iced” with an asterisk, so check its terms for exclusions.
points: Pret says you subscribe and claim in the Pret app. It is a monthly subscription, so check how to cancel before you join.

expect: 50% off up to five hot or iced

entries.name: Boots Advantage Card
entries.summary: Boots publishes how its Advantage Card works in its terms and conditions. We couldn't read these pages automatically, so no figures are shown here.
links: Boots – Advantage Card terms and conditions

entries.name: Superdrug Health & Beautycard
entries.summary: Superdrug's own page says you earn points on your Superdrug shopping in store and online once your free Health & Beautycard is registered.
points: You earn 1 point for every £1 you spend, plus more on bonus point offers for selected products or days.
Points are spent in multiples of 100: 100 points = £1, and you can use them as part-payment in store or online.
Register the card online (or with a form in store) and show it at the till; for online orders, register it on your Superdrug account.
Superdrug lists other member benefits too, such as free standard delivery on orders over £20 (£25 for non-members) and member prices on selected products.

entries.name: Argos and Nectar
entries.summary: Argos's help centre says you can collect and spend Nectar points at Argos, in store and online.
points: You collect 1 point per £1 you spend at Argos.
500 points are worth £2.50 when buying products through Argos.
Online, you need to link your Nectar card to your Argos account; in store, have your Nectar card to hand at the till.
Argos says points show in your Nectar account within 30 days.

expect: 1 point per £1 you spend at Argos

groups.title: Student discount services
groups.intro: Pointers to the student discount services themselves. We don't list individual brand discounts or codes here.

entries.name: UNiDAYS
entries.summary: A student verification service that lists discounts from many brands. Each brand sets its own offer and terms, so check the brand's page.

entries.name: Student Beans
entries.summary: A student verification service that lists discounts from many brands. Each brand sets its own offer and terms, so check the brand's page.

entries.name: TOTUM
entries.summary: The official site of the TOTUM student card. Check it for current discounts and the card price.
